s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of bilateral nasal obstruction, facial pain, and diplopia with abducens nerve palsy
salient_findings: Binocular horizontal diplopia with left lateral gaze
Inability for the left eye to track beyond the midline
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
Presented with bilateral nasal obstruction
Thick nasal discharge
Facial pain and pressure
Condition recalcitrant to 3 prior surgeries, immunotherapy, and medical therapy
Binocular horizontal diplopia with left lateral gaze
Inability for the left eye to track beyond the midline
Left eye non-proptotic, non-ecchymotic, and non-tense
Normal bedside intraocular pressure measurements
National Institutes of Health stroke score of 1
Workup results negative for cerebrovascular accident

shortlist.label: abducens nerve palsy
shortlist.why_kept: patient presented with binocular horizontal diplopia and inability for the left eye to track beyond the midline

shortlist.label: nasopharyngeal sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: patient presented with bilateral nasal obstruction, thick nasal discharge, and facial pain, which are common symptoms of nasopharyngeal sarcoidosis

shortlist.label: sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: patient presented with bilateral nasal obstruction, thick nasal discharge, and facial pain, which are common symptoms of sinusitis

shortlist.label: multiple sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: patient presented with diplopia and abducens nerve palsy, which can be symptoms of multiple sclerosis

shortlist.label: acute disseminated encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: patient presented with sudden onset of neurological symptoms, including diplopia and abducens nerve palsy, which can be symptoms of acute disseminated encephalomyelitis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of binocular horizontal diplopia with left lateral gaze and inability for the left eye to track beyond the midline are consistent with abducens nerve palsy, which is further supported by the clinical images showing left-sided abducens nerve palsy immediately following surgery and its resolution by postoperative day 1

rejected.label: nasopharyngeal sarcoidosis
rejected.why: No evidence of systemic symptoms or granulomatous inflammation

rejected.label: sinusitis
rejected.why: Although the patient has sinus symptoms, they do not explain the abducens nerve palsy

rejected.label: multiple sclerosis
rejected.why: No other symptoms or findings suggestive of demyelinating disease

rejected.label: acute disseminated encephalomyelitis
rejected.why: No evidence of widespread neurological deficits or encephalitis
